decisions.reason: A classic lever handle line built on the firm's core design, materials and fixing know-how has a long architectural lifecycle, and the firm can interpret its sales well enough to refine it rather than withdraw it, even though it was absent from the website in 2020 to 2021.

This multi-model handle family draws directly on established competencies and certified systems, so it remains easy to assimilate and adapt, and its lower web visibility more likely reflects routine catalogue status than failure.

A single handle design close to the core offer costs little to keep, but its narrow scope and absence from the website make it a plausible candidate for range pruning like Product E, so withdrawal risk is somewhat higher.
Like C, this design fits the firm's ergonomic expertise and is cheap to maintain, though as a single design without recent visibility it is more exposed to portfolio consolidation.

The flagship electronic access system anchors the strategic move toward digital building organization, and in-house R&D gives the firm the absorptive capacity to keep developing it rather than drop it.
